objective.text: Authorize private-channel membership instead of treating an obscured channel name as access control.

difficulty.rationale: Enforce subscription permission rather than relying on hard-to-guess channel identifiers.

runtime.sapi: Isolated CLI Laravel harness unless another context is explicitly stated
runtime.errorPolicy: E_ALL; UTC; no external services or application data

stem: Order updates contain private customer data. Channel names use long random order tokens, but any logged-in user who learns a token must still be denied unless they own that order. What enforces this requirement?

options.text: Use a private channel and an authorization callback that checks the authenticated user against that order.
options.rationale: The private-channel authorization endpoint must decide resource membership before approving the subscription.

options.text: Use a public channel with a longer random token and no ownership callback.
options.rationale: Secrecy of the channel identifier is not the required access-control decision once the token is known.
options.misconception: Secrecy of the channel identifier is not the required access-control decision once the token is known.

options.text: Hide the subscribe button for nonowners while keeping the channel authorization callback unconditional.
options.rationale: A direct subscription request can bypass presentation controls.
options.misconception: A direct subscription request can bypass presentation controls.

options.text: Approve every authenticated subscriber because login alone identifies an owner.
options.rationale: Authentication establishes identity but not ownership of this specific order.
options.misconception: Authentication establishes identity but not ownership of this specific order.
